title: Platoon
build: PAL disk, side 1 OVL1 at its hand-over to $0400

records.c: Entry to the tunnel section: masks CIA interrupts, sets the video bank, screen and charset, banks out the ROMs, points the IRQ vector at $271A with a raster line of $14, clears the score digits and play counters, then shows the title sequence ($B72F).

Start of play in the tunnels, reached from the title at $B6CA: draws the screens, sets the colours, puts the player on the map at $408C+$0B facing up ($09CD=$24, $09D0=6), centres the crosshair, gives nine rounds ($3E97), sets morale ($C000=$47) and fills the object table at $19D1.

Main loop, once per frame flag $09D1: moves the walking bob through $0882/$08DB, reads the joystick ($09F1), redraws the map arrow, copies the crosshair to the sprite table, and runs the enemy, message and sound updates.
Frames until the next ambush step, from $14 down.
Ambush steps until an attack, from 8 down.
Crosshair X before it is copied to $0B52.
Crosshair Y before it is copied to $0B53.
Step through the walking bob table, 0 to $51.

Times the attacks in the tunnels while the player walks dry tunnel: counts down $0720 and $0721, and after enough steps starts a Viet Cong attack through $C301, from ahead if a wall or water is near, otherwise from a side passage ($07F9 left, $0820 right). Spots marked in $084A attack from the side as soon as the player reaches them.
Frames to wait before ambushes resume after one ends.
Counts attacks; every fourth comes from ahead whatever is there.
Flags the steps of $0720 where a side attack can start.
X drift of the crosshair's walking bob, one byte per step.
Y drift of the walking bob.
Leftover data, never used.
After a wall stops the player, tries each direction in turn (north, east, south, west) until one is open, then turns the map arrow and centres the crosshair.
Set while an attack is under way.
Set when the attacker has been shot.
Map arrow character, $21-$24 by facing.
Frames since the player last moved.
Set when the player moved this frame.
Facing direction: 0, 2, 4, or 6.
Set by the interrupt each frame.
Frames between steps while the joystick is held.
No direction held: resets the step delay so the next push moves at once.

Reads the joystick: diagonals are ignored, forward steps the player in the facing direction, back steps the other way, and left and right turn; while an attack is on the stick moves the crosshair instead.
Left: turns the player anticlockwise (map arrow $21-$24), or during an attack moves the crosshair left.
Right: turns the player clockwise, or during an attack moves the crosshair right.
Back: during an attack moves the crosshair down.
Forward: steps the player ahead ($0EE5), or during an attack moves the crosshair up.
Set when fire was pressed this frame.
Crosshair X.
Crosshair Y.
Not in a room: fire shoots ($0DAF).

Fire in a room: the exit corner turns the player back into the tunnels ($0969); shooting the figure of the room 0 event scores 1000 points and ends it; otherwise the crosshair is checked against each object box of the room ($0BD6).
Tests the crosshair against each object box of the room; a hit shows the object's message and takes it.
Object 0: the first find is the flares ($0D52), the second the second flare pack ($0D53).
Object 1: the compass ($0D54).
Marks the object taken ($12), plays the pickup sound, and scores 500 points.
Object $10: an ammunition box refills the magazine to nine rounds.
A stray rts byte, never reached.
Medical supplies: heal a wound ($0CF6).
Object 3: the exit. With the flares, the second flare pack, and the compass, scores 30,000 points and goes to the dugout ($1A21); otherwise a message says what is missing.
Object $11: a medical kit heals one wound, giving back $12 points of morale and redrawing the wound marks.
Set when the flares are found.
Set when the second flare pack is found.
Set when the compass is found.
Index into the room's box table, two bytes per box.
Index into the room's object table.
Moves to the next object box; at the end of the room's boxes shows the "nothing here" message.

Fire in the tunnels: uses a round, sprays the crosshair, and if it is over an attacker in range scores 300 points and plays the attacker's death ($C301): a near attacker ($09CC 6-8) or a far one (9-12).
Every second frame plays the gunfire sound and shakes the crosshair by the table at $2282.
Two spare bytes.
Clears the view flags and scans the map in the facing direction through the drawer table $0EDB.

High byte of the scan's jump target, patched by $0ED4.
A stray rts byte after the scan's jump.
Address of the scan for each facing.
High byte and the other facings' scan addresses.
Every second call, looks up the view drawer for the facing $09D0 in the table at $0F1D, draws the tunnel view ($10A0), and if nothing blocked the view advances the wall frame $109F.
Low byte of the step's call target, patched by $0EFF.
High byte of the step's call target, patched by $0F05; the step then checks whether the view advanced.

Set while the player stands in water (map character 3), cleared on dry tunnel (2).

Returns without moving.
Moves the player one square west on the map if the square is tunnel (2) or water (3), then scans ahead for water, walls, and side passages to set the view flags.
Set when the scan finds something that stops the wall frame advancing.

Scrolls the map window when the player nears its edge: sideways at columns 3 and $10, up or down by twelve rows at the top and bottom.

Finds which of the ten rooms the player stands in by matching the map pointer, column, and map window against $1859-$1881, notes the room's object ($19D1) and hotspot box ($1891/$1931), shows its message if it has no object box, and copies the room picture (from $17EB by the room's kind) onto the screen. High byte of the second half's colour destination; the loop steps every destination down a row after each 20 characters, until 180 are drawn, then starts the room 0 event if it is due.
Sets up the sprite shapes and positions for the room event from $17F3, $1812, and $181C.

Steps the room 0 event by its timer: changes the sprites at frames $0F and $32, calls $C298 at $50, adds 500 points ($3DEC five times) and redraws ($3E37) at $96, and ends at $BE.

Message number of each object box, eight per room; the number also says what the object does: 0 flares, 1 compass, 3 the clear exit, $10 Viet Cong ammunition (refills the magazine), $11 medical supplies (heals a wound), $12 an object already taken; the rest (poetry, a table, cold tea, a diary, and so on) only show their message.

Start of the night in the dugout, reached once the tunnels are left with the flares, the second flare pack, and the compass (and from the title at $B6CD after a lost life there): resets the sprites, crosshair, morale, flares, and rounds, sets the dawn countdown at $3DC9, draws the dugout from $BD00, shows "Night has fallen, and you are in a dugout" and the warning that the Viet Cong will attack, then runs the dugout loop.

Dugout loop, once per frame at raster $AA: counts down to dawn ($3DC9/$3DCA); at zero shows "Well done! Section completed", scores 5000 points, and goes to the end screen ($B6DE); otherwise moves the crosshair ($1F34), fires ($2008), and speeds up the enemies as time passes.

Bunker frame: moves the crosshair sprite with the joystick within its box, flickers the flash colour, plays random distant gunfire through $EE19, then updates enemies ($2367), the flare ($1E50), and the morale check ($1D55).
Running sum used to pick when distant gunfire sounds.
Ends the bunker when $3F0A reaches 4 ($3BB7); after $1E hits shows a message and takes morale.
Count of hits taken in the bunker.
On the flare key, if a flare is left ($3ECE) and none is burning: takes one ($3E99), plays the launch sound, and starts the flare's climb ($1E4C) and burn ($1E4D).
Draws the rising flare on the colour screen, three rows higher each step for five steps.
Low byte of the flare's colour address, patched by $1DA5 and stepped up a row each frame by $1E26.
High byte of the flare's colour address; the routine copies it into the eight stores below.

High byte of the first store.
Low byte of the second store.
High byte of the second store; the next row of the flare follows.

High byte of the sixth store; the last row of the trail follows.

High byte of the eighth store; then the climb steps, and after five steps the trail's colours are put back.
Step of the rising flare, 0 when none.
Stage of the burning flare, 0 when none; lights the screen in stages from the tables at $1EE4.
Frames in the current flare stage, up to $32.
Returns while no flare burns.
Every $32 frames moves the flare to its next stage, setting the screen colours, enemy visibility, and sprite colours from $1EE4-$1F2C; after stage 9 the dark returns.
Operand of the flare's colour setting at $1E5B, patched from $1F14: the frames each flare stage lasts; the stage step follows.
A second rts after the flare's sound at $1EC0, never reached.
After the last stage: the dark returns and the enemies are hidden again.

Reads the joystick into $0306 and moves the crosshair up, down, left, and right.

Counts shots so the gunfire sound plays every third one.

On fire, saves the crosshair position and starts the burst.
Ends the burst and puts the crosshair back where it was, if it is inside the field.

While fire is held (up to $22 frames), drifts the aim with the joystick for recoil, uses ammunition ($3E50), plays the gunfire sound, and checks each of the three enemies against the crosshair; a hit sets the enemy dying and adds 300 points through $3DEC.
Crosshair X halved for hit tests.
Enemy X halved for hit tests.

Hit test of the burst against the three enemies in turn ($22A5, $22A6, $22A4): an enemy that is up, within $0A of the crosshair's Y and 5 of its halved X, starts dying, its sprite drops, and 300 points are scored.
Below the field, aiming at the flare box fires a flare ($1D7B); otherwise the burst sprays from the table at $2282.
Step through the spray table, 0-9.
Crosshair X halved, for the edge tests.
Alternates so the spray moves every second frame.

X drift of the burst for each frame.

Death frame of enemy 3.

Timer of enemy 3.
State of each enemy: 0 hidden, 1-4 rising, 5-6 shooting, 7-8 ducking, $0A leaving, $0B dying.

State of enemy 3.

Counts down to the next speed-up.

Animates the three enemies: plays the death frames of dying ones, brings hidden ones up at their next spot, steps them through rising, shooting, and ducking; a shooting enemy fires back with a sound, counts a hit on the player ($1D7A), and shows the muzzle flash. In the last minute before dawn no new enemies appear.

Operand of the enemy step at $2511, patched by $23E4 from the spot's delay: frames an enemy stays up shooting. The code after it plays the muzzle flash and the enemy's shot, counts the hit on the player, and steps on.
Operand at $258A, patched by $23E7: frames the enemy ducks before hiding; then the enemy is reset.

Steps one voice's effect: sweeps the frequency up, down, or between two values, and when the steps run out repeats it or turns it off.
Silences the SID ($D401-$D412) and clears the repeat flags at $F001 and $F002; nothing in this load calls it.
The effect number waiting to start on each voice, 0 for none.

Returns while a sample plays.
Plays the 4-bit sample at $F200 through the volume register (the scream of a death): points the NMI at $F0EC and runs CIA 2's timer A every 240 cycles, and sets $F15F to 1 while it plays.
Nine bytes after the routine, never read.
An NMI that is not CIA 2's (RESTORE) goes to $0108.
Sample NMI: plays the high four bits of the next byte and points the next NMI at $F123; stops at a byte of $FF or the end of the page run.
Sample NMI: plays the low four bits of the byte and points the next NMI back at $F0EC.
1 while the sample plays, 0 when it ends; the main loop skips the music then.
160 more 4-bit sample values before the sample at $F200; start_sample ($F09D) begins at $F200, so they never play.
The digitised sample, two 4-bit values a byte (high first), ending in $FF at $F6BE.
$3DAE reads the KERNAL ROM's vector table at this address, with the ROM banked in; the RAM here is part of the sample.
The end of the sample that starts at $F200.
A byte of the sample, bytes $F6BF-$F6BF.
The 4-bit sample of the scream, played from $F200 by $F09D, bytes $F6C0-$FABF.
The 4-bit sample of the scream, played from $F200 by $F09D, bytes $FAC0-$FC83.
$C47D reads the KERNAL ROM's vector table at this address, with the ROM banked in; the RAM here is part of the sample.
The end of the sample, bytes $FE00-$FFA0.
The KERNAL's SETLFS, called by $C404 with the ROM banked in.
The KERNAL's SETNAM, called by $C40D and $C436 with the ROM banked in.
